title: [Forecast quý 1/2025] Vehicles registered across five different types in Australia
prompt: The table below shows the number of vehicles registered in Australia in 2010, 2012 and 2014. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The table shows the number of different types of vehicles registered in Australia in three years, along with the percentage change over the entire period.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, all five categories of vehicles experienced growth in registration numbers from 2010 to 2014. Notably, motorcycles showed the most significant percentage increase, while passenger vehicles consistently dominated in terms of absolute numbers.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding the major vehicle categories, passenger vehicles were by far the most numerous in 2010, with 11 million registrations, nearly five times higher than commercial vehicles at 2.3 million. Subsequently, the number of passenger vehicles subsequently rose by 1 million every two years, resulting in a total of 13 million by 2014, representing an 18.2% increase over the four-year period. Similarly, commercial vehicles experienced steady growth, reaching 2.7 million by the end of the period, with an overall growth rate of 17.4%.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Regarding the remaining categories, there were 570,000 motorcycles registered in 2010, and this figure rose significantly to 745,000 by 2014, the highest percentage change among all categories at 30.7%. Meanwhile, light trucks saw the second highest relative growth at 23.5%, with their numbers rising from 106,000 to 131,000 over the four years. In contrast, heavy trucks showed the least significant growth, with registrations increasing modestly from 106,000 in 2010 to 423,000 in 2014 - a total increase of just 10.2%.
